Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Thomas Carlyle (author, Wikidata Q151403), died 1881; Ralph Waldo Emerson (author, Wikidata Q48226), died 1882; Charles Eliot Norton (editor, Wikidata Q2628443), died 1908. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Carlyle, Thomas, 1795-1881; Emerson, Ralph Waldo, 1803-1882; Norton, Charles Eliot, 1827-1908 [Editor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: The correspondence of Thomas Carlyle and Ralph Waldo Emerson, 1834-1872, Boston, J. R. Osgood and company, 1883, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/correspondenceof0000carl_n1h8. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 90%, 94%, 84% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Charles Eliot Norton, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
